title: Carbohydrates for training and competition
authors: Burke LM, Hawley JA, Wong SH, Jeukendrup AE
population: Review for the 2010 IOC consensus conference on sports nutrition: carbohydrate availability before, during and after exercise
findings: Carbohydrate intake during exercise should be scaled to the characteristics of the event.
During sustained high-intensity sports lasting about 1 h, small amounts of carbohydrate, including mouth-rinsing, enhance performance via central nervous system effects.

30-60 g/h is an appropriate target for sports of longer duration (the abstract states no lower bound, after its 'about 1 h' statement); events longer than 2.5 h may benefit from up to 90 g/h, and products with blends of different carbohydrates may maximise absorption at such rates.
Whether additional 'train-low' strategies improve performance in well-trained individuals is unclear.
limitations: Narrative review for a consensus conference, so graded D here (the grade follows the design: an expert narrative, not a systematic search); the abstract states no lower bound for 'longer duration'; it says only 'about 1 h' for small amounts and 'longer than 2.5 h' for up to 90 g/h.
implications: A grade D narrative review gives 30 to 60 g/h for events longer than about 1 h (lower bound not stated) and up to 90 g/h above 2.5 h. It names no band for 1 to 2 h specifically, so it gives no rate for a half marathon under 2 h.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (J Sports Sci 29:S17-S27). Abstract read on Europe PMC. Crossref lists no correction, erratum or retraction notice (checked 2026-11-16).
